// A family is declared once by "//= FAMILY <TAB> after PASS STAGE [<TAB> guard CONDITION] <TAB> what
// it is for" and runs after the text pass PASS, the families after one pass in the order of their
// STAGE numbers (gaps of 10 leave room between). A word on which the guard is false tries none of
// the family's rows. Its rows are ID <TAB> SPEC <TAB> CONDITION <TAB> ACTIONS

// PRIO whose condition holds applies its actions. "//~ MAP <TAB> FROM=TO ... <TAB> what it is for"

column3: The subject form of a pronoun before 가 (내가, 제가, 네가, 누가).
The subject forms back to the plain pronoun, before a particle that is no subject (나를).
The verb wishes (たい, たく, たかっ).
A subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the word in its clause.
An object を in the clause of the word, after it before a verb or before it after a subject or topic.
The verb describes no noun after it, but a formal noun of noun.clause, and no verb follows it in the sentence but an auxiliary of its て form.

A dictionary word that is the passive of a dictionary verb, read with 어지다, 되다, a potential or an honorific, which no Korean reader uses with an object; not before いる, whose 어 있다 the active verb cannot take (知られている 알려져 있다).

A passive verb that no Korean passive word reads yet (an analysed passive, or a dictionary word that is the passive of a dictionary verb read with 어지다, 되다, a potential or an honorific: 使われた 사용되었다, 見られた 볼 수 있었다), with a person before に as its agent an object of を in its clause and no subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the に, is the act of that person: the に is the subject (이)가, with a pronoun in its subject form, and the verb is active, a dictionary word being written as its verb (弟に手紙を破られた 남동생이 편지를 찢었다, 父に傘を使われた 아버지가 우산을 사용했다, 俺に頭を撫でられる 내가 머리를 쓰다듬는다). Not without an object (母に叱られた 어머니에게 야단맞았다), nor when the verb describes a noun after it that is no noun.clause (彼女に別れ話を切り出された情けないヤツ keeps the passive) or another verb that is no auxiliary of its て form follows it in the sentence (吸われ、自らも吸血鬼化した keeps the passive).

When the verb is an act one was made to do (forced-act) and no adverb of adverb.forcing stands in the clause, the 억지로 of that act follows it (母に野菜を食べさせられた 어머니 때문에 억지로 야채를 먹었다).

column3: A causative-passive verb (読まされる, a dictionary row of verb.causative-passive, or させられ after a noun) after a causer that causer-ni read 때문에 억지로, or 때문에 with an adverb of adverb.forcing in the clause, not one that asks or denies, which is the potential, nor one of something one goes through (undergone-verb), is the act one was made to do: the active verb (母に本を読まされた 어머니 때문에 억지로 책을 읽었다, 父に勉強させられた 아버지 때문에 억지로 공부했다). Without a causer it stays 게 되다. The させられ after a noun reads 하게 되다 (L4554: 心配させられた 걱정하게 되었다), after a noun of something one undergoes whose Korean takes 당하다 (ko-noun.cp-danghada) it is 당하다 (解雇させられた 해고당했다), after one that takes 받다 (ko-noun.passive-batda) 받다 (検査させられた 검사받았다), and after a noun of a change that befalls one (noun.cp-change) with no object を before it in its clause it is 되다 (孤立させられた 고립되었다). A causative-passive whose ending already says 게 되다 (ことになる) drops its own (読まされることになった 읽게 되었다, 退院させられることになった 퇴원하게 되었다).

column3: What stops the search from a giver before に to its verb: a particle of another role, a mark, or a verb that is no adjective in く.

The してもら read 받다 (지도를 받다, 설명받다) is 해 주다 when a person before it, with に read 에게 and no other に, no は, が or から, no verb but an adjective in く and no punctuation between, does it for the speaker, with no subject or topic (が, は, も, って) before the person in the clause: the giver then becomes the subject (benefactive-provider). Not right after a verbal noun of noun.receive-verbal, whose 받다 is one Korean verb (紹介してもらった 소개받았다). After an adverb, an adjective in く or a verb in ように with no object を before it, it is 해 주다 too (優しくしてもらった 다정하게 해 주었다), but not after よく (잘 대접받다). A もら read 달라고 하다 (a request) after a causative is the plain 주다: the causative asks leave, not a favour (見極めさせてもらおう).

column4: A もら or もらえ after a causative in て with no person but the speaker in に before it is the speaker's act with leave (spec GRM-44). A もら that ends the sentence goes into the verb's ending: 겠습니다, 겠다, 겠어 (わ, よ, ぞ), 게요, 게 (ね) for the present, the plain past for もらった and 었어 for もらったよ and もらったわ (やらせてもらいます 하겠습니다, 読ませてもらった 읽었다). So does the ます of a word of verb.permission-word (使わせてもらいます 사용하겠습니다). A もらえ or いただけ in ますか or ませんか asks leave: 어도 될까요, the speaker in に before it the subject; after another person in に it asks that person, 게 해 주실 수 있을까요 (俺にやらせてもらえますか 내가 해도 될까요; permission-request has the causatives that hold もらえませんか or いただけ). The guard keeps the rows, whose doer check scans the clause, off every word but もら, もらえ, いただけ and those of verb.permission-word.

column3: A と (or と、) left as (와)과 or nothing right after a predicate that ends in one of ending.final-quote quotes what was said or thought before it: after an ending in 다 its indirect form, 고 (見たいんだと 보고 싶다고), asked with 냐고 where a question word stands before it in its sentence (何があったんだと 무슨 일이 있었냐고), after another ending the direct quote 하고 (熱いんじゃないかなぁと想像して 뜨겁지 않을까 하고 상상해), and nothing where it ends the sentence or an ellipsis follows (どうかと… 어떨까…). An ending in 니다 is quoted directly too. Before a word of word.partner-to (同じ, 同時, 一緒) the と after a plain past or たい is the comitative and stays (死んだと同時に); after a sentence particle it still quotes (そうだねと一緒に笑った).

column3: The polite form of an exclamation in 구나.

A polite present copula (です, a tic of it such as でち or っす; not でした, whose past the word would have to take) after an interjection or adverb whose Korean is already a whole utterance (ありがと 고마워, ごちそうさま 잘 먹었어, なるほど 그렇구나) or after a verb in a て form read in its bare 어 form that is no compound particle (手伝って 도와; not について) adds no 이다 right after it (not after an ellipsis: お任せください……です): after 해체 it is 요 (고마워요, 잘 먹었어요), an exclamation in 구나 takes its polite form or stays (그렇군요), and after a polite ending, also of a word with the prefix お (おやすみ 잘자요), it is dropped (죄송합니다).

The している after a word in と says the state it names, not an act. A と word read as the 하다 verb of a 하다 adjective of ko-adjective.hada-state is that adjective, conjugated with the ending of いる (堂々としている 당당하다, 堂々としていた 당당했다, 堂々としている人 당당한 사람); after an adverb in 히 or 게 it is the adverb with 있다, without 하고 (じっとしている 가만히 있다).

column3: What ends the search from a condition to its main clause: a quote, a sentence end, or a clause that ends in a comma and no condition.

A ば or たら condition read (으)면 before a main clause in the past is one that did not hold, (았)더라면: a condition of ている or of ない (an adjective or いない, not the copula でなければ) in ば before a sentence that ends in the past (降っていなければ 오지 않았더라면, 君がいなければ 네가 없었더라면), and any ば or たら before a sentence that ends in a past with のに, かもしれない, だろう or はず (来れば間に合ったのに 왔더라면, 違っていたら刺さっていたかもしれない), unless the condition is one of seeing, saying or thinking (傍から見れば). A verb negated in ば (来なければ) takes it only before a sentence that ends in a past negative, a past of いい or such a supposition (来なければ乗ることもなかった 오지 않았더라면), not before a plain past of what followed (開けなければ並んだ). A quote (と, って), a clause that ends in a comma and no condition, or the end of the sentence stops the search, so a condition inside what is thought keeps (으)면; so do an obligation (なければならない) and a condition after と (としたら) or before a list in も (もいなければ).

column3: A plain polite question ますか that ends the sentence, after a verb of doing with no question word before it, offers or proposes the act only on a positive sign: a confirm-dialog action (word.confirm-action: 上書きしますか？ 덮어쓰기할까요?, 回復薬を使いますか), a choice with にする (お風呂にしますか 목욕으로 할까요), asking what to do (どうしますか, いかがいたしますか), or a cue of an offer before it in the sentence (word.offer-cue: さて、帰りますか 자, 돌아갈까요; お茶でも飲みますか): 까요. column3: The humble 参る and まいる of the speaker. Its present ます that ends a sentence goes: 가겠습니다 (白雲、参ります！ 백운, 가겠습니다!); its past comes to where the listener is: 왔습니다 (スウェーデンから参りました 스웨덴에서 왔습니다); its ましょう goes along: 갑시다. After a て form the present goes on doing it, 어 가겠습니다 (徹底してまいります 철저히 해 가겠습니다), but after an errand of verb.errand it is going to do it and coming back, 어 오겠습니다 (お茶を淹れてまいります 차를 끓여 오겠습니다).

column3: The word before is a pronoun of the listener, alone or with a plural suffix (お前, 貴公ら).
A recipient in に before the word in its clause that is the listener (お前に, 貴公らに).
A に before the word in its clause after anything but a pronoun of the listener (みんなに, 彼女に).
The speaker as subject or topic before the word in its clause (私が, 俺は).
A word of word.inclusive before the word in its sentence, up to the verb before (一緒に, われらの).

The volitional read 자 of a verb of giving to someone (verb.grant: 授ける, 与える, 教える, 見せる, 許す, and あげる read 주다) that ends the sentence, not after a て form, with the listener in に (pronoun.listener), the speaker as subject, or an object in its clause in speech (before a closing bracket or an exclamation mark), and no other recipient in に and no word of word.inclusive in its sentence, is the speaker's will to the listener, not an invitation: 주마, the verb in 어 with 주마 when its Korean is not 주다 already (力を授けよう 힘을 내려 주마, いいことを教えよう 좋은 것을 가르쳐 주마, 私が許そう 내가 용서해 주마). ならない or いけない follows the condition.

A quote (と, 、と, って) takes the condition.
The sentence or the line ends after the condition, or a pause ends the utterance.
Nothing that the condition could lead to follows it.

column3: The comma is a pause before a particle, の, the copula or みたい that still belong to the predicate before it (嬉しい、です), not before a conjunction of word.clause-start (でも).

After the comma a new clause starts: a demonstrative adverb or conjunction of word.clause-start (そう思った, でも), a demonstrative pronoun of word.clause-pronoun with が, は, も or を (それが), a conjunction or an interjection, or a predicate that ends its clause right there, before a mark, the end or a particle that joins clauses, and holds no subject of its own (転がる、転がる。, 汚い、弱いからだ).

A bare attributive verb or adjective (the present 0 of a verb, the past 8 of a verb, the 4 of an adjective in い) right before a comma ends its clause when a new clause starts after the comma (comma-clause): the terminal form 다 (わからない、それが人生だ 모른다, 그것이 인생이다, よくわからない、でも行く 잘 모른다, 하지만 간다). Before a noun phrase it describes, even one with は or も (映画館の中で食べた、ポップコーンは 먹은, 팝콘은), it stays attributive (ドアの内側に設置された、鈴の音 설치된, 방울 소리), and so before a particle, の or the copula after a pausing comma (嬉しい、です).

The first predicate after the word in its sentence asks, tells, wishes, tries or makes (verb.youni-purpose): the ように says what is aimed at.

A ように of a verb read 도록 or 게 is a likeness, not an aim: 것처럼 before a verb of seeming (verb.youni-seem: 泣いているように見えた 울고 있는 것처럼 보였다, 騙そうとしているようには見えなかった 속이려 하고 있는 것처럼은 보이지 않았다), 것처럼 after ている when the first predicate after it does not ask, tell, wish, try or make (殴られているように頭が痛む 맞고 있는 것처럼 머리가 아프다; 待っているように言った keeps 도록), and 듯이 after まるで or あたかも in its sentence (まるで許しを請い跪くように 마치 용서를 빌며 무릎 꿇듯이) or when the first predicate after it is a gesture, a look, a voice or a touch (verb.youni-depicted) and the verb before it is one a person does: not a potential, a passive, a verb of what happens (verb.youni-unwilled) or 있다, 되다, 받다, with no が subject or なるべく before it (からかうように笑った 놀리듯이 웃었다; 目線を合わせるようにしゃがむ keeps 도록). After a noun, かのように and かのような are 인 것처럼 and 인 것 같은 (子供かのように 아이인 것처럼).

column3: The ほしい (欲しい) of a wish.

The verb before is a て form that the rules read as 기를 or 면 for ほしい, not the blank ある of であって nor a main ある or いる of a state (こうあってほしい 이랬으면 좋겠다), which no one does for the speaker; the auxiliary of ている is (待っていてほしい 기다리고 있어 줬으면 한다).

The ほしい after a て form wishes someone did something: 아 줬으면 좋겠다 (早く来てほしい 빨리 와 줬으면 좋겠다, 教えてほしいのだけれど 가르쳐 줬으면 좋겠는데), 주었으면 좋겠다 after a verb that already gives (てくれて), not 기를 원하다 or 면 좋겠다; it keeps 하다 where it describes a noun or is past (見てほしいもの 봐 줬으면 하는 것, 来てほしかった 와 줬으면 했다). Denied, てほしくない and ないでほしい are 지 말았으면 좋겠다 (見てほしくない 보지 말았으면 좋겠다, 行かないでほしい 가지 말았으면 좋겠다).

column3: The など opens a line or follows a sentence end or a pause.

A など that opens a line or follows a sentence end or a pause, right before a quoting と, takes up what was said before it, not a list: its と is 하고 where the word stage read it as the companion (와)과, and the など adds nothing (察しろっての！などと、内心でボヤく 눈치채라고! 하고, 속으로 투덜대다). After anything but a noun (a closing bracket, a predicate), before a verb of thinking or saying, など+と reads the same way (「嘘だ」などと叫んだ 「거짓말이다」 하고 외쳤다); before と言 it is 같은 말을, keeping the voice (「嘘だ」などと言った 「거짓말이다」 같은 말을 했다). After a list of nouns など keeps its 등 (りんごやみかんなどと言った 사과나 귤 등이라고 말했다).

column3: A listing particle (や, とか, やら, ・) or a comma or と between nouns inside the noun phrase that ends before the word (りんごやみかんなど, 本、雑誌など).

The word says no: the negative ない standing on its own or fused with いる (ない, いない), a verb that carries the negative (しない, 買わない, せずに, しません), a negative ending (ません, ず, ぬ), 無い, 無し, 皆無, or a word the rules read with a Korean negative (하지 않다, 필요 없다, 안 되다, 리가 없다); not an adjective that ends in ない (つまらない) nor a condition of what one must do (しなければ).

column3: A predicate of word.dismissal that is not itself denied (嫌いではない).
The word says no or brushes something aside (word.dismissal: 嫌い, どうでもいい).
The clause of the word goes on into another one: it describes a noun after it (食べない人) or ends in a condition, a reason, an aim or a nominalizer (しないと, しないので, しないように, 起きないこと).
A word that says no and closes the clause.
The word says that something is not there and closes the clause: ない, 無い, いない, 皆無, 無し, ありません, いません, ございません, 存在しない (the scan that looks for one stops at a predicate before it).
The word refuses by a rhetorical question (信じるものか, 負けるもんか).
The sentence ends after the word.

column3: The clause ends: a comma, a sentence end, a quote or concession (でも, だって, って, と), a reason, or a predicate that ends in a condition, a concession or a reason.

The word follows a single noun the rules read (not a listing, nor a question in か: 誰かなんて, nor a formal noun after a predicate: わからないことなんて), and no comma, quote (などという, なんて言う, なんて呼ぶ) or も, は written with the next word follows it.
A predicate in わけ or はず that is denied, after が or も or right after it, in its own ending or in the words after it (見つかるはずもない, 申し出られるわけがない): it cannot be.
A が of another subject (記憶がない), not of わけ, はず or こと (わけがない).

The sentence asks: a question mark, or a final か that is no rhetorical ものか (飲みませんか？, 質問などございませんか。).

column4: A など, なんか or なんて right after a single noun (no listing before it in its noun phrase, no particle after it) belittles the noun when its clause ends in a predicate that says no or brushes the noun aside (spec LEX-90, LEX-91); a negative inside a clause that goes on (食べない人, しないと, しないように, 起きないこと) or in a question is no such end. Before a rhetorical refusal (ものか, もんか) all three are 따위 (言葉なんか信じるものか 말 따위 믿을까 보냐). A など is 같은 건 before a predicate that says the noun is not there or cannot be (余地などない 여지 같은 건 없다, 理由など見つかるはずもない 이유 같은 건 발견될 리도 없다), 같은 건 in narration and before a passive or respectful predicate (予算など議論されなかった 예산 같은 건 논의되지 않았다), and 따위 before any other that says no (言葉など信じない 말 따위 믿지 않는다), not the listing 등. A なんか or なんて that the word stage read as the topic (은)는 or as 같은 것 there is 같은 건 (神なんか信じない 신 같은 건 믿지 않는다). After a noun and に (spec LEX-92) なんか and なんて write 따위 before that particle: 따위가 before なる (退学になんかならない 퇴학 따위가 되지 않는다), else 따위에. Not before a quote (なんて言う) or before する.

column3: The word ends a sentence that asks nothing: no question mark after it, nor か, の, って, と or で.
An adverb of a thing found to be so as expected (adverb.realization: やっぱり, 結局, ほら) before the word in its sentence.

After an adverb of a thing found to be so (adverb.realization: やっぱり, 結局) a sentence-final んじゃない that asks nothing affirms it, not a negation (spec MNG-9): the 거 아니야 of a predicate is 거잖아 (やっぱりあんたがやったんじゃない！！ 역시 네가 한 거잖아!!, 結局興味あるんじゃない 결국 흥미 있는 거잖아) and a noun's (이)가 아니야 is (이)잖아 (やっぱりツンデレなんじゃない！ 역시 츤데레잖아!). The いいんじゃない that asks nothing (좋잖아) is the pack row negf:iinja. A question (帰ったんじゃない？ 돌아간 거 아니야?) and a sentence with no such adverb keep their reading (俺が悪いんじゃない 내가 나쁜 게 아니야).

column3: A verb whose Korean is decided by one word it is paired with, where the sense table cannot see the pair: 潜む shares its stem with 潜る and is 숨다 (奥底に潜むもの 깊은 속에 숨는 것); a passive 揉まれる after a noun of waves and に is 휩쓸리다 (波に揉まれてきた 물결에 휩쓸려 왔다); 変わった before a person is 특이하다 (変わった人 특이한 사람, 彼は変わった人だ), unless what changed stands right before it with が, a comparison with と or an adverb of change does (性格が変わった人, 昔と変わった人, すっかり変わった人); 見る after 夢 and a particle that stresses or limits it (は, も, ばかり, でも and the like) is 꾸다, while 夢に, 夢で and 夢として are where one sees (夢ばかり見ていた 꿈만 꾸고 있었다, 夢で見た 꿈에서 봤다); 悪い before と or とは and a verb of thinking, with nothing, punctuation, an opening bracket, a conjunction, an adverb, a first-person pronoun with は or も, or a clause in のは or のが before it, is the speaker's regret 미안하다 (悪いと思ってる 미안하다고 생각해); after another noun it says what is bad (体に悪いと思う). 後にする after を is leaving that place, 떠나다 (部室を後にした 동아리방을 떠났다, その場を後にした 그 자리를 떠났다); after a task, talk or matter it stays 뒤로 하다 (宿題を後にして, その話を後にしよう). つける right after けじめ and a comma is 짓다, the pair the sense table reads without the comma (けじめ、つけたい 매듭, 짓고 싶다).

column3: A か right after a predicate whose ending holds a quoting と (read 다고, 라고) lists what is said, or reports it vaguely: the か is 든가 in the place of the 고 (浮気してるとか 바람피우고 있다든가, 50倍だったとか 50배였다든가); a だとか read (이)라고 is (이)라든가, unless it is だと before かなり (麻薬の類だとかなり危ない) or reports what was heard before 聞く (迷信だとか聞いた 미신이라고 들은). A か that ends the sentence after a quotation in って asks about what was said: 다는 건가, after a quoted order 라는 건가, and after a noun (이)라는 건가 (寝られないってか 잘 수 없다는 건가, ハーレムってか 할렘이라는 건가). A ってか after a pause, ahead of a comma, takes back what was said: 그보다.
